title: The Xerox Alto put a page-shaped display on a desk
body: Introduced as a research computer in 1973, the Alto used a portrait graphics display of 606 by 808 pixels. A mouse and keyboard let its user work with information shown on the screen.
takeaway: A tall display suited documents that people already thought of as pages.
source: Computer History Museum, Xerox Alto Source Code
visual: an early desktop computer with a tall blank monochrome display and a wired mouse

title: An early CD-ROM product was an encyclopedia
body: Philips and Sony announced the CD-ROM format in 1984. A disc could hold about 550 megabytes of prerecorded data, and in 1985 Grolier released an electronic encyclopedia on the format.
takeaway: A format designed around reading a disc with a laser could distribute reference material as well as music.
source: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History, Memory and Storage
visual: a reflective compact disc beside a closed reference book with a blank spine
